Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and for the details. Short answer up front: we can provide Redwood tax docs (W-9) and an invoice stub, but the exact invoice of record depends on the marketplace and whether the purchase was transacted as "Seller of Record" by the cloud vendor or as a co-sell/reseller flow.

Quick summary by marketplace (high level):
- Azure: often lists Microsoft as the billing entity; Redwood can provide a vendor invoice/receipt that your AP team can attach for internal records, and we can provide a W-9. For Azure marketplace "transactable" listings where Microsoft is the seller of record, tax reporting to the buyer is via Microsoft and we may need a PO amendment to have Redwood as seller of record.
- AWS: usually offers both AWS-billed or Marketplace Metering (AWS as seller) and in some cases Sellers of Record can be the ISV.
- GCP: similar but fewer co-sell/marketplace permutations — typically GCP bills and we provide supporting vendor docs.

Laura (billing ops) — can you add the canonical language and attach the standard W-9 and an invoice stub for the AH-789 order? Karthik, flag anything about partner/co-sell that would change the buyer-facing docs.

I'll follow up with a short checklist for Sarah's AP team so they can route the PO amendment if needed.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — Laura from Billing Ops here. Apologies for the delay — wanted to make sure I gave you precise guidance. Long-ish, but wanted to be explicit so your AP team has a checklist.

1) US purchases via Azure Marketplace (common scenarios)
   - Microsoft as Seller of Record (SOR): Azure issues the invoice and collects payment. Redwood is the partner/ISV. In this case we can issue a "vendor supporting invoice" that contains our Redwood line items and tax id (EIN), but the legal invoice of record will remain Microsoft. Your AP can attach both documents (Microsoft invoice + Redwood supporting invoice) to the payment. Redwood will also provide a W-9 (attached).
   - Redwood as Seller of Record (less common): If the transaction is configured so Redwood is SOR, Redwood will issue the invoice and handle tax reporting. That requires a marketplace listing configuration change and a PO amendment — we can support this but it is a procurement/legal change that takes time.

2) VAT / International flow (UK example)
   - If the UK subsidiary is billed by Microsoft (Microsoft SOR), Microsoft will handle VAT invoicing and collection. Redwood can provide a VAT registration statement or certificate to support your VAT reclaim process, but we cannot change the invoice Microsoft issues unless we become SOR.
   - If Redwood is SOR (for the UK invoice), we will issue a VAT invoice with our VAT number; this again requires the marketplace listing to be configured for Redwood as seller and changes to the sales order.

3) Practical next steps for AH-789
   - I attached a Redwood invoice stub that mirrors the Azure invoice lines. Use this for your internal GL and attach the Microsoft invoice for audit trail.
   - I also attached our W-9 (W9_Redwood.pdf). Please confirm where to upload vendor paperwork (some enterprises use a vendor portal, others want DocuSign).
   - If you want Redwood listed as seller of record going forward, we should schedule a short procurement/legal sync; I'll include Marissa (channel/partnerships) for co-sell implications.

Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_Billing_FAQ.pdf, W9_Redwood.pdf, Azure-Invoice-Sample-AH-789.pdf

Let me know if you want a one-pager for AP that describes which documents to attach for audits.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
